purpose: the bare-deposit probe — can this project land ANY proof-requiring transaction? tx A could not, and four causes were ruled out for free first.
list: register + OpenChannel + OpenSubchannel + Deposit-to-note — four actions, one value-moving

resourceBounds.note: sized from the 78,047,360 l2 that tx A actually consumed, not guessed

whyNotRelayed: the relayer wire has no resourceBounds field, so every relayer submission goes through a fee estimate that cannot see the proof and reverts. It is structurally unable to submit a value-moving pool transaction today. Keeping the same self-submit mechanism as tx A also makes the shorter list the only changed variable.
result: LANDED — the first proof-requiring transaction this project has ever put on mainnet
gasComparison: the SUCCESSFUL probe consumed 88,071,920 l2 gas — MORE than the reverted tx A consumed (78,047,360) — under a 150M bound. Independent reconfirmation that tx A did not run out of gas: it stopped 22M short of its own cap while a heavier list succeeded.
leadingCauseForTxA: tx A used `.deposit({ amount })` with NO recipient. The SDK's own swap example uses the recipient-less form to declare an OPEN note — a note whose amount a LATER deposit writes. So tx A most likely created an unmatched open note that nothing deposited into, which is the pool's UNDEPOSITED_OPEN_NOTES trap. Day-0 verification recorded that `compile_actions` CANNOT catch this — it no-ops the open-note emission — which is exactly why the client compiler and the prover both accepted a list the chain rejected. The probe used `.deposit({ recipient, amount })`, a real note, and succeeded.
